title: Canonical Frobenius comparison identifies ordinary cohomology pullbacks
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the finite coefficient ring $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, with $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $n\geq1$, of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $Y_0$ be proper of finite type over $k_0$, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and fix $m\geq1$. Write $\Phi_Y$ and $g_Y$ for the scheme and geometric Galois Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. On the small pro-etale site use derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and ordinary cohomology [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Specify $\kappa_{m,Y}:L(\Phi_Y^m)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g_Y^m)^*$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] by the factorization $\Phi_Y^m=g_Y^m\operatorname{Fr}_Y^{(q^m)}$ of [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], the canonical pullback-composition identification [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and the multiplicative absolute-Frobenius trivialization [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. Let $d_\Phi:L(\Phi_Y^m)^*A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Y$ and $d_g:L(g_Y^m)^*A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Y$ be the canonical constant-sheaf identifications. Then $d_g\circ\kappa_{m,Y,A_Y}=d_\Phi$.

For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $h=\Phi_Y^m,g_Y^m$, let $\rho_{h,M}:R\Gamma(Y,M)\to R\Gamma(Y,Lh^*M)$ be ordinary cohomology pullback, induced by the pullback/direct-image adjunction unit [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the canonical identification of global sections of a direct image with global sections on the source. Then
$$
R\Gamma(Y,\kappa_{m,Y,M})\circ\rho_{\Phi_Y^m,M}=\rho_{g_Y^m,M}.
$$
This is an equality of morphisms in $D(A)$, natural in $M$, with the canonical constant section $1$ preserved by the comparison.

source.place: Step 1: normalization on constant coefficients and identification of the induced ordinary cohomology maps

proof.text: Put $b=am$, $F=\operatorname{Fr}_Y^{(q^m)}=F_Y^b$, $P=\Phi_Y^m$ and $G=g_Y^m$. By [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], $F=g_\sigma^mP$; composing with the inverse $G$ gives $P=GF$. Use the normalization in the statement of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]: on sheaves the absolute-Frobenius comparison $\tau:F^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ is adjoint to the direct-image identification induced by the relative Frobenius isomorphisms $r_V=(F_V^b,v):V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_{Y,F}Y$. Thus the ordinary module pullback comparison is $\theta_M=\tau_{G^*M}\circ c^{\mathrm{sh}}_{F,G,M}:P^*M\to G^*M$, where $c^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is canonical module pullback composition. All these module pullbacks are exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations].

source.place: Step 1: identification of the functors and of the units

proof.text: The termwise comparison induced by $\theta$ is precisely the specified $\kappa_{m,Y}$. Indeed, choose a K-flat representative with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. On that representative [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies the specified derived composition map with the termwise ordinary module comparison. The statement of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] specifies that its derived trivialization is induced termwise by the same relative-Frobenius sheaf trivialization, including the $b$-fold iterate. Therefore the two comparisons agree on every K-flat representative. Naturality along its quasi-isomorphism to the original complex, followed by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](3), gives equality on the derived category.

source.place: Step 1: identification of the functors and of the units

proof.text: Write $d_H^{\mathrm{sh}}:H^*A_Y\to A_Y$ for the canonical module coefficient identification, for $H=F,G,P$. The right-adjoint identification used to define $\tau$ sends a section on $V\times_{Y,F}Y$ to its restriction along $r_V$. Its inverse therefore sends every constant section $a\in A$ to the same constant section $a$. On $A_Y$ this inverse equals the structure map $A_Y\to F_*A_Y$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]: the two agree on the constant presheaf, hence agree after sheafification by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Taking adjuncts, using the characterization of the canonical adjoint comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], gives $\tau_{A_Y}=d_F^{\mathrm{sh}}$. In particular the comparison fixes $1$; it is not chosen only up to a scalar.

source.place: Tag 0F6W (lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale), with the adjoint normalization specified in lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback

proof.text:
The coefficient identification for $P=GF$ is $d_P^{\mathrm{sh}}=d_F^{\mathrm{sh}}\circ F^*(d_G^{\mathrm{sh}})\circ c^{\mathrm{sh}}_{F,G,A_Y}$. To check the normalization of this formula, the adjunct of either side sends $a\in A$ to the constant section $a$ after the two base changes: this is exactly the definition of the coefficient structure map in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and sheafification uniqueness gives equality. Naturality of $\tau$ for $d_G^{\mathrm{sh}}$ now gives
$$d_G^{\mathrm{sh}}\circ\theta_{A_Y}=\tau_{A_Y}\circ F^*(d_G^{\mathrm{sh}})\circ c^{\mathrm{sh}}_{F,G,A_Y}=d_P^{\mathrm{sh}}.$$
Apply this equality termwise to the coefficient complex in degree zero. Step 2 identifies the resulting comparison with $\kappa$, proving $d_g\circ\kappa_{m,Y,A_Y}=d_\Phi$.

source.place: Step 1: identification of the functors and of the units

proof.text:
For an $A_Y$-module sheaf $N$, write $e_{H,N}:\Gamma(Y,N)\to\Gamma(Y,H^*N)$ for the adjunction section map. A global section $s$ is the module map $\widetilde s:A_Y\to N$ sending $1$ to $s$ (its inverse sends a module map to the image of $1$). The module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with the coefficient map normalized as in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], identifies $e_{H,N}(s)$ with $H^*(\widetilde s)\circ(d_H^{\mathrm{sh}})^{-1}$. Explicitly this is the adjoint of the unit applied to $\widetilde s$, evaluated on the constant section $1$ of the terminal base change. Naturality of $\theta$ and step 4 therefore give
$$\theta_N\circ P^*(\widetilde s)\circ(d_P^{\mathrm{sh}})^{-1}=G^*(\widetilde s)\circ\theta_{A_Y}\circ(d_P^{\mathrm{sh}})^{-1}=G^*(\widetilde s)\circ(d_G^{\mathrm{sh}})^{-1}.$$
Hence $\Gamma(Y,\theta_N)\circ e_{P,N}=e_{G,N}$ as $A$-linear maps, not just on constant coefficients.

source.place: Step 1: identification of the functors and of the units

proof.text:
Represent $M$ by a K-injective complex $I$ of $A_Y$-modules, and choose a K-injective resolution $j_G:G^*I\to J$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small pro-etale site. Put $j_P=j_G\circ\theta_I:P^*I\to J$. Exact pullback in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] means these termwise complexes represent $LP^*M$ and $LG^*M$; $j_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism because both factors are. Step 5 in every degree gives an equality of chain maps
$$\Gamma(Y,j_P)\circ e_{P,I}=\Gamma(Y,j_G)\circ e_{G,I}:\Gamma(Y,I)\to\Gamma(Y,J).$$
Apply [lem-trf-proetale-unit-leray-chain-formula] to $(P,I,J,j_P)$ and $(G,I,J,j_G)$. Its left side uses the identical source and target comparisons for both maps; its right side is the derived-unit definition of $\rho$ followed respectively by $R\Gamma(j_P)$ and $R\Gamma(j_G)$. Since $j_P=j_G\theta_I$, cancel the common isomorphism $R\Gamma(j_G)$ to obtain $R\Gamma(Y,\kappa_{m,Y,M})\circ\rho_{P,M}=\rho_{G,M}$ in $D(A)$, using step 2. These maps are natural in $M$ by naturality of the derived adjunction unit, the canonical section identification and $\kappa$. Step 4 gives the required preservation of $1$.
